### Q1
No. Moving the store to SQLite (node:sqlite) was rejected because ops backs up data/store.json with a nightly rsync job that diffs plain-text files, and a binary SQLite file would break those checks. The store must stay a plain-text JSON file. Write speed is handled by debouncing writes in src/store.ts.

### Q2
Yes, src/legacy/ must not be modified. The platform team's sync job overwrites that folder every Monday, so any change would be silently lost. Separately, docs/erp-api.md is owned by the ERP team and must not be edited.

### Q3
The HMAC-SHA256 signature goes in a top-level `sig` field in the JSON body. It is computed over the compact JSON without `sig`, and `sig` is appended as the last key. It's enabled by the env var ERP_WEBHOOK_SECRET, and if that's unset the payload goes out unsigned. We first tried an X-Signature header, but the ERP API gateway strips all custom X- headers, so the ERP saw every request as unsigned (verified on staging).

### Q4
Port 9911, since the October infra move. docs/erp-api.md and the README still say 8080, which is outdated, and config/default.json erp.url also still says :8080.

### Q5
Every new user-facing error `message` must be in German, because the warehouse staff UI shows them verbatim to packers. The `code` stays English SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE. Old English messages are left as they are.

### Q6
Austrian public holidays are a hardcoded list in src/services/holidays.ts, covering 2026 and 2027 only. It's hardcoded because the deployment has no outbound internet. The list must be extended before 2028, and other years silently get no holidays.

### Q7
No. The ERP answers 422 to any array payload, so it accepts only one event object per request. The batching idea (arrays of up to 50 per POST) was a dead end and must not be built.

### Q8
No new npm dependencies are allowed, runtime or dev, because each package needs a security review of about 6 weeks.

### Q9
Yes, and it's a dead end. A memoized version, written elsewhere (probably QA's build), showed stale list ETAs after a new tracking event, and a correct cache key got messy. Our calculateEta is computed fresh per request, and the regression test 'list eta is never stale' covers it. Measurements showed no upside anyway: ETAs for 50 items take about 0.4 ms.

### Q10
There are 3 attempts in total with a fixed 30 s delay and no backoff. Retries happen only on network errors, timeouts and 5xx, not on 4xx, and each attempt sends the same payload. The ERP dedupes by event_id only within 2 minutes, and the worst case is 75 s, which fits inside that window.

### Q11
Never log recipient name, address or phone, in any log line, because they are personal data under GDPR (the DPO flagged this in last month's audit). Shipment IDs and tracking numbers are OK to log.

### Q12
Yes: 'emits webhook on delivered' in test/events.test.ts (OPS-412, owned by the platform team). If it fails, rerun once and do not fix it.

### Q13
ATP tracking numbers are validated as UPU S10 with a check digit (src/lib/s10.ts, code INVALID_TRACKING_NUMBER). All other carriers accept any non-empty value. Carrier formats change often, and valid DHL numbers were wrongly rejected for 2 days last year. The check lives in the shared validateShipmentInput, so POST /import validates ATP numbers too.

### Q14
fs.watch never fires on staging, because the config is a Docker bind mount from a Windows host and file change events don't propagate into the container. fs.watchFile (polling) worked. Hot reload is a future need and nothing has been built yet.

### Q15
Yes, GET /shipments/:id. Its response must not change in any way (no added, removed or renamed fields), because mobile app v2.3 parses it with a strict schema and crashes on unknown or missing fields. The next mobile release is in January. `shipmentToApi()` is shared by list, detail and POST, so changes have to be made per endpoint, not in that function.
Nothing in that message qualifies for the ledger. It was a recall quiz, and it stated no new rule, decision, dead end or fact.

## Mission
- Feature work on parcel-tracker: Node 24 runs TS directly (no build step), zero dependencies. User works autonomously-by-default and reviews everything at the end. Nothing is committed yet (all work is uncommitted in the working tree).

## Rules
- (user) NEVER modify anything under src/legacy/ — the platform team's sync job overwrites the folder every Monday, so changes are silently lost.
- (user) NO new npm dependencies, not even dev deps — each package needs a ~6-week security review.

- (user) Flaky test: 'emits webhook on delivered' in test/events.test.ts (OPS-412, platform team owns it). If it fails: rerun once, do NOT fix.

## Decisions
- Store perf: keep JSON file, debounce writes in src/store.ts (mutations within 200 ms => ONE write) + a flush method for shutdown — because save() rewrote the whole file per mutation and got slow at a few thousand shipments. (user)
- Austrian public holidays are a hardcoded list in src/services/holidays.ts, 2026+2027 only (list must be extended before 2028; other years silently get no holidays) — because the deployment has no outbound internet. (user)

(user) The check lives in the shared validateShipmentInput, so POST /import validates ATP too.

(user)

## Dead ends
- fs.watch for hot-reloading config/default.json → never fires on staging: the config is a Docker bind mount from a Windows host, file change events don't propagate into the container. fs.watchFile (polling) worked. Hot reload is a future need, nothing built yet. (user)
